images.description: Screenshot of the Wired article 'Pentagon Kills LifeLog Project' (Feb 4 2004) — DARPA's cancelled program to build a database tracking a person's entire existence. Paired in Q lore with Facebook's founding the same day.
images.text: WIRED STAFF. BUSINESS. 02.04.04 12:00 PM. PENTAGON KILLS LIFELOG PROJECT. THE PENTAGON CANCELED its so-called LifeLog project, an ambitious effort to build a database tracking a person's entire existence. Run by Darpa, the Defense Department's research arm, LifeLog aimed to gather in a single place just about everything an individual says, sees or does: the phone calls made, the TV shows watched, the magazines read, the plane tickets bought, the e-mail sent and received. Out of this seemingly endless ocean of information, computer scientists would plot distinctive routes in the data, mapping relationships, memories, events and experiences.

images.description: Reuters article (April 19, 2018): 'Man linked to 9/11 attacks on U.S. captured in Syria: Pentagon' — Mohammad Haydar Zammar, a Syrian-born German national, captured by Syrian Democratic Forces; a red oval highlights the sentence 'The Syrian Democratic Forces are an alliance of militias in northern and eastern Syria.'
images.text: REUTERS. WORLD NEWS. APRIL 19, 2018 8:42 PM. Man linked to 9/11 attacks on U.S. captured in Syria: Pentagon. WASHINGTON (Reuters) - A man linked to the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks on the United States, who was said to have praised violent jihad, was captured in Syria by U.S.-backed forces more than a month ago, the Pentagon said on Thursday. We can confirm that Mohammad Haydar Zammar, a Syrian-born German national, was captured more than a month ago by SDF (Syrian Democratic Forces) partners as part of their ongoing operations to defeat ISIS inside Syria, Pentagon spokesman Eric Pahon said. The Syrian Democratic Forces are an alliance of militias in northern and eastern Syria. We are working with our SDF partners to obtain additional details, Pahon said. The 9/11 Commission report, a Congressional account on the 2001 attacks, said Zammar was an outspoken, flamboyant Islamist who extolled the virtues of violent jihad. It said Zammar reportedly had taken credit for influencing Ramzi Binalshibh, who is accused of wiring money to September 11 hijackers and passing information to al Qaeda operatives, and Mohammed Atta, who led the attack on the World Trade Center in New York City. U.S. officials have said that there are hundreds of foreign fighters and thousands of Syrian Islamic State militants in SDF custody. Reporting by Idrees Ali.

images.description: Annotated excerpt of page 2 of a May 21, 2018 letter from Senator Ron Johnson to FBI Director Christopher Wray, quoting two January 8, 2017 emails by then-FBI Deputy Director Andrew McCabe. A red arrow and red box highlight the email subject line 'Flood is coming,' and 'McCabe' is underlined in green. The quoted emails discuss CNN being close to running a 'sensitive story' and were sent to FBI leadership and to Sally Yates and Matthew Axelrod.
images.text: The Honorable Christopher Wray. May 21, 2018. Page 2. Excerpt of:. Letter from Senator Ron Johnson to FBI Director Wray. January 8, 2017, 12:08 p.m. Then-FBI Deputy Director Andrew McCabe sent an email to senior FBI leadership with the subject line "Flood is coming." Mr. McCabe wrote, "CNN is close to going forward with the sensitive story. . . . The trigger for them [CNN] is they know the material was discussed in the brief and presented in an attachment."8. January 8, 2017, 12:55 p.m. Mr. McCabe emailed then-Deputy Attorney General Sally Yates and then-Principal Deputy Attorney General Matthew Axelrod with the subject line "News."9 Mr. McCabe wrote, "Just an FYI, and as expected, it seems CNN is close to running a story about the sensitive reporting."10
flags: Annotations (arrow, box, underline) added by an unknown poster to emphasize 'Flood is coming'

images.description: Screenshot of a 4chan post by Q (tripcode !ITPb.qbhqo, 11/09/17, No.148782302) attaching a file named '_AF1_5A_2.png', shown with its thumbnail and the full image below: a photograph taken through an aircraft window at altitude over ocean, with layered clouds, sunset light, and several small islands visible below. The filename implies it was taken aboard Air Force One during Trump's November 2017 Asia trip; the location is not identifiable from the image.
flags: The claim that the photo was taken from Air Force One rests only on the filename and Q context; the aircraft and location cannot be verified from the image.

images.description: Photograph taken through an aircraft window at high altitude, looking down past scattered cumulus clouds at a hazy sea with several small dark islands and a sunlit horizon band at dusk or dawn. No landmarks are identifiable. The original Q filename '_AF1_5A_3.png' implies the photo was taken aboard Air Force One; nothing in the image itself confirms the aircraft or the location.
flags: Filename implies the photo was taken from Air Force One - unverified

images.description: Elevated photograph looking down on the Supertree Grove at Gardens by the Bay in Singapore, with its distinctive purple-red tree-like vertical garden towers, elevated walkway, surrounding gardens, domed conservatory roofs and greenery. Apparently taken from a high vantage such as the Marina Bay Sands SkyPark. The filename 'SING_CLAS_P_L1' was read by followers as signalling Q/POTUS presence in Singapore around the June 2018 summit. No text in the image.

High-angle aerial photograph of Gardens by the Bay in Singapore, apparently taken from the Marina Bay Sands tower: the two shell-shaped conservatories (Flower Dome and Cloud Forest), Supertree Grove, the Dragonfly Lake, and Marina Barrage across the reservoir with cargo ships in the strait beyond. Filename 'SING_CLAS_P_L2' ties it to Q's Singapore photo series posted around the June 2018 Trump-Kim summit.

Dusk photograph of the Singapore central business district skyline and Marina Bay, taken from high up behind a glass balustrade etched 'DO NOT LEAN AGAINST THE GLASS' — a vantage consistent with the Marina Bay Sands SkyPark. Lit towers include signage for Citi, Maybank, OUE, Straits Trading and CapitaGreen; the Fullerton Hotel sits at the waterfront. Filename 'SING_F2F_LOCK_TOP' framed the image in the drop as proof of presence in Singapore ahead of the June 2018 Trump-Kim summit ('F2F' = face-to-face).
images.text: DO NOT LEAN AGAINST THE GLASS. CITI. OUE. STRAITS TRADING. THE FULLERTON
flags: The drop's implication that this was taken by a Q insider ahead of the summit is unverifiable; the photo itself only shows the Singapore skyline

images.description: Elevated daytime photograph (framed as a phone screenshot with black bars) looking over the Singapore skyline, apparently taken from a high hotel or office window. The three towers and SkyPark of Marina Bay Sands are visible on the distant left horizon; the foreground shows white stepped office/hospital-style blocks, a tower with a red logo, and residential high-rises amid greenery. Posted by Q with the filename 'Specx', implying a firsthand vantage in Singapore around the June 2018 summit.
flags: Exact vantage building and date not shown; the implication that Q took the photo is unverified

images.description: Dusk photograph, framed as a phone screenshot, taken from the rooftop infinity pool of the Marina Bay Sands hotel in Singapore, looking along the pool edge toward the lit-up port and city below. Swimmers line the pool's edge; palm trees and loungers at left. Filename 'MBS_KIM1' ties it to Q posts presenting it as an original photo around the June 2018 Trump-Kim Singapore summit.
flags: Association with the Trump-Kim summit comes from filename/post context; swimmers are unidentified private individuals

images.description: Dusk photograph (letterboxed phone screenshot) taken from the rooftop infinity pool of the Marina Bay Sands hotel in Singapore, with swimmers at the pool's edge, palm trees and loungers at left, and the lit-up port/industrial waterfront of Singapore far below. Filename ‘MBS_KIM2’ ties it to the June 2018 Trump–Kim Singapore summit context.
flags: Swimmers are anonymous private individuals

images.description: Night-sky webcam frame from SkunkBayWeather.com, timestamped June 10, 2018, 03:56:14 AM, showing a bright vertical streak of light rising through clouds over Puget Sound in Washington State. The image circulated as evidence of an alleged missile launch near Whidbey Island; Q posted it in that context. Investigators and the U.S. Navy denied any launch, and analyses attributed the streak to a helicopter's light trail in the long exposure.
images.text: SkunkBayWeather.com Jun 10, 2018 03:56:14 AM. Temp: 47.7°F, Wind: SE at 4 mph, Gust: 8.0 mph, Pressure: 30.0 in, Rain: 0.20 in
flags: The 'missile launch' interpretation is unverified and widely debunked; the streak is most plausibly a helicopter light trail in a long-exposure frame

images.description: Decode graphic linking three documents about the June 2018 DOJ Inspector General report. Left: a June 14 2018 Congress of the United States letter to DOJ Inspector General Michael Horowitz signed by Reps. Andy Biggs, Ron DeSantis and Matt Gaetz, expressing concern that 'people may have changed the report in a way that obfuscates your findings' and requesting the original drafts. Right top: Q drop of 06/13/18 (No.1739449) claiming POTUS possesses original and modified versions of the IG report, with 'Modified IG redacted report [RR version]' underlined. Right bottom: a @realDonaldTrump tweet of 5 Jun 2018 hoping the report 'is not being changed and made weaker'. Red lines connect the underlined passages, implying the letter and tweet corroborate the drop's altered-report claim.
images.text: ANDY BIGGS. 5TH DISTRICT, ARIZONA. HOUSE JUDICIARY COMMITTEE. 1626 LONGWORTH HOUSE OFFICE BUILDING. COMMITTEE ON SCIENCE, SPACE, AND TECHNOLOGY. Congress of the United States. House of Representatives. Washington, DC 20515-0305. June 14, 2018. Michael Horowitz. Inspector General. U.S. Department of Justice. 950 Pennsylvania Avenue, N.W. Suite 4706. Washington, D.C. 20530-0001. Dear Inspector General Horowitz, Almost one month ago, your office completed its draft report reviewing the Department of Justice (DOJ) procedures in the Clinton email investigation. A draft was circulated to people within the DOJ and Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), providing an opportunity to respond and rebut the report's findings in the final stage before the details become public. Your team has worked to ensure that this report is thorough and accurate; however, an investigation of this magnitude and consequence deserves heightened scrutiny to guarantee that the process has not been compromised in any way. The trust of the American people depends on it. We are concerned that during this time, people may have changed the report in a way that obfuscates your findings. Per Congress's oversight authority, we request you supply your original drafts along with the final published form. Unfortunately, over the past year, the DOJ has repeatedly fought requests by Congress to produce documents related to this investigation, and when the DOJ actually provided documents, the materials have been heavily redacted. Past and present DOJ officials have asserted security concerns, even though the documents we have seen do not legitimately contain these issues. We have every confidence that your investigation and report has been thorough and accurate. We request the various drafts of the report, particularly the draft provided to the DOJ and FBI, before those agencies made any changes to the draft report, be provided to us. Thank you for your time and your service to our country. Sincerely, Andy Biggs. Member of Congress. Ron DeSantis. Member of Congress. Matt Gaetz. Member of Congress. Q !CbboFOtcZs 06/13/18 (Wed) 22:50:25 ID: 8d9246 No.1739449. POTUS in possession of (and reviewing): 1. Original IG unredacted report. 2. Modified IG unredacted report [RR version]. 3. Modified IG redacted report [RR version]. 4. IG summary notes re: obstruction(s) to obtain select info (classified). [#3 released tomorrow]. [SEC: FBI/DOJ handling of HRC email investigation]. [[RR]]. Who has the sole ability to DECLAS it all? Did you witness the stage being set today? Nunes/Grassley/Freedom C. push for docs. [[RR]] central figure within docs (personally involved). KNOWN CONFLICT. Immediate impeachment / resignation / termination / recusal IF EVER BROUGHT TO LIGHT. Be loud. Be heard. Fight for TRUTH. Q. Donald J. Trump. @realDonaldTrump. Follow. What is taking so long with the Inspector General's Report on Crooked Hillary and Slippery James Comey. Numerous delays. Hope Report is not being changed and made weaker! There are so many horrible things to tell, the public has the right to know. Transparency! 3:38 AM - 5 Jun 2018

For a member of the legal profession it is the highest of honors to serve on this Court. Please permit me by this letter to express my profound gratitude for having had the privilege to seek in each case how best to know, interpret, and defend the Constitution and the laws that must always conform to its mandates and promises. images.text: SkunkBayWeather.com  Jun 10, 2018  03:56:14 AM. Temp:  47.7°F, Wind: SE  at    4 mph, Gust:  8.0 mph, Pressure:  30.0 in, Rain: 0.20 in
flags: The missile-launch interpretation is unverified and was widely disputed; a helicopter long-exposure light trail is the commonly accepted explanation

images.description: Phone screenshot of a tweet (author handle cropped out of frame) commenting on the August 2018 arrest of a man before a Trump rally in Wilkes-Barre, Pennsylvania. The tweet includes a photograph of a Press Enterprise newspaper front page dated Thursday, August 2, 2018, headlined 'TRUMP ATTACK FOILED', reporting that Jeffrey Gardner Boyd, 55, of Tulsa, Oklahoma was arrested in Briar Creek, PA with a loaded pistol after allegedly threatening President Trump and his family; the article says an unidentified local woman he had met on Twitter alerted police. The tweet's author implies she is the 'Mystery Woman' referenced in the article.
images.text: This "Mystery Woman" would really like to hug OUR FAVORITE PRESIDENT. I'm sure @SecretService would have stopped this guy too but I'm glad I got him off the streets before you arrived. See article below ~ Part 2 next tweet. Beattie, Hubberd and McDermott Obituaries Page 4. Thursday, August 2, 2018. $1. TRUMP ATTACK FOILED. Oklahoma man drove here with loaded gun, police say. By LEON BOGDAN Press Enterprise Writer. BRIAR CREEK - An Oklahoma man was arrested here and is being held in lieu of $1 million bail for allegedly threatening to assassinate President Donald Trump and his family. He was taken into custody and his weapon confiscated Tuesday after he had driven here nonstop to meet a local woman with whom he had discussed politics on Twitter, arrest papers say. Trump is scheduled to appear at a rally this evening in Wilkes-Barre. Alerted by the woman of the threat to the president, State Police began searching for Jeffrey Gardner Boyd, 55, of Tulsa. Troopers from the Shickshinny barracks found him Tuesday afternoon, parked at the Giant Foods store. Inside his vehicle they found a loaded Springfield .45-caliber pistol and two extra magazines, both full, police said. Mystery woman. Boyd is reported to have said that he drove nonstop from Oklahoma to Columbia County to meet the woman. She is a Trump supporter and had posted pro-Trump remarks, which he had been following on her Twitter account in recent days, arrest papers say. Police did not publicly identify the woman. She told authorities that Boyd told her he feared she "may be in danger." Boyd also told her the CIA was "sending messages directly into his head," and that he was hearing "voices" telling him to kill Trump as well as Donald Trump Jr., Ivanka Trump and her husband, Jared Kushner. Please see TRUMP page 6. JEFFREY GARDNER BOYD. When heroin was medicine. Accused. Very Happy Alaskan and 7 oth...

images.description: Widely published magazine photograph (early 1970s) of Gloria Vanderbilt sitting on a brass bed in a pink-gingham-wallpapered bedroom, reading a book to her two young sons in blue striped pajamas holding stuffed animals — the boys are Anderson Cooper (per the filename 'A_Cooper29195') and his brother Carter Cooper. Mounted on the wall above the bed is a folk-art triptych/altarpiece with a dark-robed crowned female figure over a small reclining figure, flanked by angels, a sun panel and a moon panel. Q-community sharing of this image centered on claims that the artwork is occult; the image itself is a family/interiors photo shoot.

images.description: Photograph of a drained, vintage indoor swimming pool lined with cream-colored tile under a barrel-vaulted brick ceiling, lit by underwater-style lights; ropes hang from a railing above the deep end and a wooden ladder stands mid-pool. Consistent with the widely photographed indoor pool of the Biltmore Estate in Asheville, North Carolina. The photo circulated in Q-adjacent threads with sinister insinuations about the hanging ropes, which the estate describes as period safety ropes.
flags: Location identification is probable, not confirmed in-image
Sinister interpretations of the ropes are circulating claims; the mainstream explanation is period safety equipment

images.description: Composite of two images. Left: photograph of the historic indoor swimming pool at the Biltmore Estate, Asheville - an empty white-brick vaulted pool room with candles, a wooden ladder, planters, and knotted safety ropes hanging from a rail, which circulated online with claims the ropes were nooses. Right inset: a painting of seven pale girls and young women in swimsuits standing in a row against a white-tiled wall with hands clasped, consistent with the style of Serbian painter Biljana Djurdjevic, whose work Pizzagate proponents linked to such photos. The juxtaposition implies the painting depicts the pool room.
flags: The implied connection between the pool photo and the painting is an unverified conspiracy claim; the 'nooses' in the Biltmore pool photo are reported by the estate to be period safety ropes; painting attribution is probable, not certain

images.description: Photograph of a figurative painting: five pale, doll-like girls in white leotards and bright red shoes sit in a row on a dark bench against a yellow-and-blue tiled wall, mouths open, staring forward. The style and subject are consistent with Serbian painter Biljana Djurdjevic, whose works were reported to hang in Tony Podesta's art collection; the filename ‘Podesta Art Red Shoes’ carries that claim into Pizzagate/red-shoes symbolism threads.
flags: Attribution to Djurdjevic/Podesta collection is inferred from circulation context and filename, not shown in the image

images.description: Product-style photograph of an ornate silver-tone charm necklace displayed on a white jewelry bust against a grey-green background. The long chain carries pearl-like beads and small figural charms (birds and other animals), ending in a large medallion pendant: a central coin bearing a left-facing male profile, ringed by smaller coins and topped by bird figures, with three chain drops below ending in fish charms and a small figure. The central coin's profile is consistent with an Imperial Russian coin (Tsar Nicholas II style) but is not certainly identifiable from the photo.
flags: Central coin identity uncertain — profile consistent with an Imperial Russian coin but not confirmed

The juxtaposition implies a connection between red shoes, these figures, and the McCann case without stating one.
images.text: MAGA. Disappearance of Madeleine McCann. Madeleine Beth McCann disappeared on the evening of 3 May 2007 from her bed in a holiday apartment in Praia da Luz, a resort in the Algarve region of Portugal, sparking what one newspaper called "the most heavily reported missing-person case in modern history". Her whereabouts remain unknown. More at Wikipedia.

According to a DS official, shortly after the memorandum was delivered, Secretary Clinton approached the Assistant Secretary and told him she “gets it.” The use of personal email accounts to conduct official business has been a particular concern over the past several years. Following the March 2011 memorandum, DS cybersecurity staff conducted two cybersecurity briefings of S/ES staff, the Secretary's immediate staff, and Bureau of Public Affairs staff in April and May 2011. OIG discovered in Secretary Clinton's retired paper files a copy of the classified presentation used during the briefing. It contains material similar to the type provided in the March 11, 2011, memorandum. On June 28, 2011, the Department, in a cable entitled "Securing Personal E-mail Accounts" that was approved by the Assistant Secretary for Diplomatic Security and sent over Secretary Clinton's name to all diplomatic and consular posts, encouraged Department users "to check the security settings and change passwords of their home e-mail accounts because of recent targeting of personal email accounts by online adversaries."141 The cable further elaborated that "recently, Google asserted that online adversaries are targeting the personal Gmail accounts of U.S. government employees. Although the company believes it has taken appropriate steps to remediate identified activity, users should exercise caution and follow best practices in order to protect personal e-mail and prevent the compromise of government and personal information." It then recommended best practices for Department users and their family members to follow, including "avoid conducting official Department business from your personal e-mail accounts."142

images.description: Scan of an October 24 2017 letter on Perkins Coie letterhead from general counsel Matthew J. Gehringer to William W. Taylor III of Zuckerman Spaeder, releasing Fusion GPS from confidentiality obligations regarding Perkins Coie's identity. A red box highlights the closing disclosure that Fusion GPS approached Perkins Coie in March 2016 and, aware the firm represented the DNC and 'Hillary for America', was engaged to continue research on candidate Donald Trump that Fusion GPS had begun for other clients during the Republican primary - the engagement behind the Steele dossier.
images.text: PERKINSCOIE. 131 South Dearborn Street Suite 1700 Chicago, IL 60603-5559. +1.312.324.8400 +1.312.324.9400 PerkinsCoie.com. Matthew J. Gehringer MGehringer@perkinscoie.com D. +1.312.324.8655 F. +1.312.324.9655. October 24, 2017. VIA EMAIL. William W. Taylor, III Zuckerman Spaeder LLP 1800 M Street, NW Suite 1000 Washington, DC 20036. RE: FUSION GPS. Dear Mr. Taylor: I write on behalf of Perkins Coie LLP as its General Counsel. We understand that your client, Fusion GPS, has received a number of requests for information regarding the identity of clients who engaged Fusion GPS to conduct research during the 2016 Presidential campaign. We further are aware that Fusion GPS is currently engaged in litigation in the United States District Court for the District of Columbia in an effort to prevent the compelled disclosure of its bank records which would reveal confidential client information. We recognize the important principle of client confidentiality, and we appreciate your efforts to fulfill your obligation to maintain client confidentiality. In the circumstances, however, we believe it is appropriate to release Fusion GPS from this obligation as it relates to the identity of Perkins Coie. Further, given the interest in this issue, we believe it would be appropriate for all parties who hired Fusion GPS in connection with the 2016 presidential campaign to release Fusion GPS from this obligation as well. Finally, now that the appropriate client representatives have been informed of the specifics of our engagement with Fusion GPS, and with their consent, Perkins Coie therefore authorizes you to disclose the following: -- Fusion GPS approached Perkins Coie in early March of 2016 and, aware that Perkins Coie represented the Democratic National Committee ("DNC") and HFACC, Inc. ("Hillary for America") with respect to the 2016 elections, expressed interest in an engagement with the Firm in connection with the 2016 presidential election to continue research regarding then-Presidential candidate Donald Trump, research that Fusion GPS had conducted for one or more other clients during the Republican primary contest.

images.description: Scanned statement from President Donald Trump on the National Strategy for Counterterrorism, bearing his signature. The statement announces approval of the strategy, cites efforts against ISIS in Syria and Iraq, withdrawal from the Iran nuclear deal, and increased defense funding, and calls the document the first fully articulated counterterrorism strategy since 2011.
images.text: Statement From The President. On The National Strategy For Counterterrorism. As your President, I am committed to protecting the United States and its interests abroad from the threat of terrorism. The National Strategy for Counterterrorism that I approved today will help protect our great Nation, enhance our national security, and guide our continued effort to defeat terrorists and terrorist organizations that threaten the United States. Under my leadership, the United States has accelerated efforts to defeat terrorists. Working with coalition partners, we have decimated ISIS in Syria and Iraq. Likewise, I ended United States participation in the horrible Iran deal, which had provided a windfall for the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and its proxies, funding Iran's malign activities throughout the world. Importantly, I have also secured historic increases in defense funding to rebuild our Nation's military. The National Strategy for Counterterrorism is an important next step. It outlines the approach of the United States to countering the increasingly complex and evolving terrorist threats and represents the Nation's first fully articulated counterterrorism strategy since 2011. It provides the strategic guidance needed to protect the United States against all terrorist threats, while simultaneously fostering the agility to anticipate, prevent, and respond to new threats. Guided by the National Strategy for Counterterrorism, we will use all instruments of American power to protect our great Nation, and we will defeat our enemies with the full force of American might.

images.description: Screenshot of an Associated Press news article dated January 7, 2019, headlined 'Ginsburg Missing Supreme Court Arguments for 1st Time'. It reports that Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg, 85, was missing oral arguments for the first time in more than 25 years while recuperating from December 21 surgery that removed two cancerous growths from her left lung, discovered while she was treated for ribs fractured in a November 7 fall.
images.text: Ginsburg Missing Supreme Court Arguments for 1st Time. By The Associated Press. Jan. 7, 2019. WASHINGTON — The Supreme Court says Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg is missing arguments for the first time in more than 25 years as she recuperates from cancer surgery last month. Court spokeswoman Kathy Arberg said Monday the 85-year-old Ginsburg is continuing to recuperate and work from home after doctors removed two cancerous growths from her left lung odn Dec. 21. Ginsburg was discharged from a New York hospital on Christmas day. Ginsburg had two earlier cancer surgeries in 1999 and 2009 that did not cause her to miss court sessions. She also has broken ribs on at least two occasions. images.description: Screenshot of a web article entry headed 'President Trump' with a cutout Getty Images photo of Donald Trump in a dark suit and red tie against a wood-grain illustration. The paragraph, bylined Abby Vesoulis, discusses Trump's use of Twitter as a presidential 'bully pulpit'. The format matches TIME's 'Most Influential People on the Internet' list (the manifest filename is 'Influential POTUS.PNG').
images.text: President Trump. Getty Images (2). FDR had the radio. JFK had TV. Trump has Twitter. The President rode to the office of the presidency on a 140-character soapbox (now 280) and has since turned it into the ultimate presidential bully pulpit. In the past, he singled out individuals as "weak" and "insecure," in addition to a barrage of personalized insults; most recently, he called Congresswoman Maxine Waters "an extraordinarily low IQ person." Sometimes, those tweets also undermine his own administration, such as when he announced a transgender military ban before the policy was implemented. And although Trump's unorthodox stream of consciousness may generate headlines and galvanize his base, it has also raised concerns among national-security officials. That could be why a majority of respondents to an Economist/YouGov poll said Trump's Twitter style is inappropriate. In November, one former contract employee working for Twitter appeared to be so fed up by Trump's online presence that he suspended the President's account on his last day of work, though he now asserts the 11-minute period where people couldn't access @realDonaldTrump's Twitter feed was a "mistake." —Abby Vesoulis
flags: outlet identified from format and filename, not shown in the screenshot

images.description: Screenshot of a web article entry headed 'Q' with an anonymous silhouette illustration (Getty Images) over a floral line-drawing background. The paragraph, bylined Melissa Chan, describes the anonymous 4chan poster Q and the QAnon conspiracy theory, noting media coverage and Roseanne Barr's tweets. The format matches TIME's 'Most Influential People on the Internet' list (the manifest filename is 'Influential Q.PNG'), and it was referenced by Q post 2772 alongside the list's Trump entry.
images.text: 'Q'. Getty Images (2). Last October, an anonymous user, known simply as Q, started posting cryptic messages on the controversial message board 4chan—the common theme being that President Trump is a secret genius and his opponents, namely Hillary Clinton and Barack Obama, are evil. Q reportedly claimed to be getting this information directly from the government, thanks to top-secret, "Q-type" security clearance. There has been little—if any—hard evidence to support Q's musings. But over time, thousands of people started to believe them—or at least, to acknowledge they might be real. And they became the foundation of a wide-ranging conspiracy theory, known as QAnon, that has been covered by the New York Times and New York Magazine, among others, and discussed in more than 130,000 videos on YouTube. One of its most prominent followers: Roseanne Barr, who tweeted several references to QAnon before being fired from her hit TV show in May. —Melissa Chan

article's characterizations of Q and QAnon are the outlet's claims

images.description: Third continuation screenshot of the Breitbart article on Lara Logan's media-bias comments, all body text with extended block quotes. Logan compares the American media landscape to the Wailing Wall's small women's section, groups Breitbart and Fox News as minority 'dissident' outlets against CBS, ABC, NBC, Huffington Post and Politico, argues media homogeneity distorts coverage (citing negative Trump coverage), and says the media have become 'political activists' and arguably propagandists.
images.text: Logan grouped Breitbart News and Fox News as dissident outlets relative to the “mostly liberal” news media landscape. She said:. Visually, anyone who's ever been to Israel and been to the Wailing Wall has seen that the women have this tiny little spot in front of the wall to pray, and the rest of the wall is for the men. To me, that's a great representation of the American media, is that in this tiny little corner where the women pray you've got Breitbart and Fox News and a few others, and from there on, you have CBS, ABC, NBC, Huffington Post, Politico, whatever, right? All of them. And that's a problem for me, because even if it was reversed, if it was vastly mostly on the right, that would also be a problem for me. My experience has been that the more opinions you have, the more ways that you look at everything in life — everything in life is complicated, everything is gray, right? Nothing is black and white. News media homogeneity cripples many people's desire for getting to the truth about political goings on, determined Logan:. How do you know you're being lied to? How do you know you're being manipulated? How do you know there's something not right with the coverage? When they simplify it all [and] there's no grey. It's all one way. Well, life isn't like that. If it doesn't match real life, it's probably not. Something's wrong. For example, all the coverage on Trump all the time is negative. … That's a distortion of the way things go in real life. Logan warned:. One ideological perspective on everything never leads to an open free diverse tolerant society. The more opinions and views … of everything that you have, the better off we all are. So creating one ideological position on everything throughout your universities, throughout academia, in school and college, in media, and everywhere else, that's what concerns me. I don't have to agree with everybody. Logan added, “Although the media has historically always been left-leaning, we've abandoned our pretense — or at least the effort — to be objective, today. … We've become political activists, and some could argue propagandists, and there's some merit to that.”. Logan cast Breitbart News as a useful barometer of “the other side” of news media:. This is the problem that I have. There's one Fox, and there's many, many, many more organizations on the left. … The problem is the weight of all these organizations on one side of the political spectrum. When you turn on your computer, or you walk past the TV, or you see a newspaper headline in the grocery store If they're all saying the same thing, the weight of that convinces you that it's true. You don't question it, because everyone is saying it. Unless you seek out Breitbart on your computer, you're probably not even going to know what the other side is saying. Most news media outlets ignore the origins of ostensibly grassroots political activism, stated Logan. She pondered the geneses of such campaigns, speculating on technology firms' roles in amplifying such campaigns:

images.description: Final continuation screenshot of the Breitbart article on Lara Logan's Mike Drop interview. Logan questions whether social-media grassroots movements are manufactured by algorithms, calls single-anonymous-source reporting 'not journalism', and says fake-news responsibility begins with journalists. She claims Media Matters for America, founded by David Brock, targeted her after her 60 Minutes Benghazi report, and recounts in graphic terms the February 2011 sexual assault she suffered in Cairo while covering Hosni Mubarak's ousting. The article closes with her quip that the interview is 'professional suicide' and a byline follow link.
images.text: We don't even question if what we see on social media is real or not. We don't even question if a grassroots movement is really grassroots. You know, there's a way to start a grassroots movement. You write an algorithm, and you create all this outrage, and you're basically throwing out all the sparks that light the fire, so then it becomes a grassroots movement because it takes nothing to set that in motion. But did it really begin as one? And if it didn't begin that way, but was manipulated and paid for by someone and serves someone's political purpose, is it really what we believe it is?. …. People were manipulated into doing that. … Who's behind it? Who's doing it, and why are they doing it? And what else are they doing? Those things are profoundly significant, and we're not even trying to find out who it is. That really bothers me. Logan dismissed news media claims allegedly rooted in singular anonymous government sources as unreliable. “That's not journalism, it's horseshit,” she said. “Responsibility for fake news begins with us,” said Logan, referring to journalists and reporters. Logan recalled for Media Matters for America (MMFA) targeted her following a 60 Minutes report she filed related to the September 11, 2012 Islamic terrorist attack on the U.S. diplomatic compound in Benghazi, Libya. “I made one comment about Benghazi,” remarked Logan, ” [then] I was targeted by Media Matters for America, which was an organization established by David Brock, who has dedicated himself to the Clintons. It was their known propaganda organization.”. In February of 2011, Logan was sexually assaulted — and nearly murdered — by numerous men in Cairo, Egypt, while reporting on the ousting of then-Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak. She shared some details of the attack's nature, including. “Piece by piece, they tore all my clothing off, and just tore my body almost to pieces, and tore my insides apart,” recounted Logan. “I saw people taking pictures. … I remember fighting, being raped, and being able to sometimes push people away, and then I remember just realizing that there were too many of them — and it was over and over and over again — and that there was always someone else when you could fight one person.”. Towards the end of the interview, Logan quipped, “This interview is professional suicide for me.”. Follow Robert Kraychik on Twitter.

Red circles and arrows connect a '14' and a symbol on the rifle to Podesta's palms, and a side panel recounts the Osiris myth (body cut into 14 pieces, phallus eaten by fish) to imply occult symbolism. The implied Podesta-shooting connection is the collage maker's claim and is not supported by evidence.

images.description: Screenshot of body text from John Solomon's March 25, 2019 opinion column at The Hill (first of a multi-part capture; no headline or byline visible). The text claims that special counsel Robert Mueller found no evidence Trump conspired with Russia, and asserts that the Steele dossier originated with Hillary Clinton, the DNC, Perkins Coie and Fusion GPS, that it was used to justify a FISA warrant on the Trump campaign, and that FBI-related leaks and Ukrainian sources fed the collusion narrative. These are the columnist's characterizations and claims, presented as opinion commentary.
images.text: Now that we know for sure that special counsel Robert Mueller, the U.S. intelligence community and Republicans on the House and Senate Intelligence Committees found no evidence that President Trump conspired with Russia to hijack the 2016 election, it is worth stepping back and evaluating the electoral impact of one of the greatest faux scandals in history. Before doing that, though, let's summarize what we now know about the origins of the investigation. Hillary Clinton and the Democratic National Committee asked their law firm, Perkins Coie, to hire the political opposition research firm Fusion GPS to dig up dirt during the 2016 election on Trump and Russia. Fusion, in turn, hired former British intelligence operative Christopher Steele, who turned to a "retired" Russian intelligence officer in the United States to get most of this dirt. Steele took his information to the FBI and senior Justice Department official Bruce Ohr to interject it into law enforcement circles and make it a criminal matter. According to Ohr, Steele was "desperate" to defeat Trump and viewed his dossier as raw intelligence that was not verified. To augment that research, the Clinton campaign had a Democratic operative working with Ukraine's embassy in Washington to research Trump's Russia ties, as well as a Ukrainian lawmaker feeding information to Fusion GPS. In another words, the main evidence used by the FBI to justify a Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA) warrant to spy on the Trump campaign in its final weeks before the 2016 election, and for much of 2017, came from a political dirty-trick operation paid by Trump's Democratic rival and run by a foreigner who disliked Trump. That operation gathered uncorroborated evidence from foreigners in Russia and Ukraine who had their own motives for influencing the election. Now, if the FBI probe ran with the secrecy of a normal counterintelligence operation, Americans never would have heard all of this, especially when the core allegations — in the Steele dossier — turned out to be bogus. But the FBI, Fusion GPS's Glenn Simpson, Steele, U.S. intelligence officials and lawmakers briefed in Congress all leaked various details to the news media, creating a furor unseen since Watergate. The only difference is, Watergate involved proven crimes by a president and the Russia-collusion narrative ultimately did not. Simpson acknowledged in a conversation with Ohr that his and Steele's last-minute contacts with reporters during the 2016 election were a "Hail Mary attempt" to influence voters.
flags: Article is opinion commentary; its claims (e.g. 'faux scandal', dossier origins, 'spy on the Trump campaign') are the author's characterizations, not established fact
Attribution to John Solomon/The Hill inferred from the accompanying tweet and filename; no byline visible in this crop

images.description: Second continuation screenshot of body text from John Solomon's March 25, 2019 opinion column at The Hill. The columnist claims law enforcement and intelligence officials privately told him there was no Trump-Russia collusion, criticizes Rep. Adam Schiff and Sen. Mark Warner for insisting evidence existed, and lists media reports he says were wrong (CNN on a Russian bank server, The New York Times on a campaign-Russian intelligence meeting, Carl Bernstein, John Brennan on MSNBC). It cites 'more than 530,000 stories' on the investigation and closes by tying the coverage to more than three dozen House Republican retirements in 2018.
images.text: Over the past two years, I have talked with law enforcement and U.S. intelligence officials who unequivocally told me they found no evidence that Trump and Russia colluded. Yes, Russia hacked Democratic emails and bought some Facebook ads to influence the election, but such activity was not coordinated with the Trump campaign. Yet, key lawmakers such as Rep. Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) and Sen. Mark Warner (D-Va.) continued to insist there was evidence of collusion, circumstantial or otherwise. They were talking to the same FBI and intelligence agencies as Mueller and I did — and that means what they said in public was not consistent with what they were told in private. But Schiff, Warner and others found a receptive audience in the news media, where misinformed or inexperienced reporters delivered a 24/7 barrage of stories intended to corroborate a collusion plot that did not exist. CNN, for example, reported there was evidence a Russian bank's servers secretly transmitted instructions to the Trump Tower. The FBI said it did not. The New York Times reported senior Trump campaign officials met with senior Russian intelligence to collaborate during the election. The FBI, Congress, U.S. intelligence and Mueller found no such meeting happened, and former FBI Director James Comey publicly debunked the newspaper report. Carl Bernstein, the reporter of Watergate fame, declared another Nixonian-sized scandal was brewing and Mueller's report would prove how Trump helped Russia "destabilize" the United States. The report did not. Former CIA Director John Brennan boldly predicted on MSNBC that Mueller had secured numerous sealed indictments. He had not. In all, more than 530,000 stories were written between May 2017 and this month about a Trump-Russia investigation that, ultimately, found no collusion. The earned media impact of that negative coverage likely would have cost billions of dollars if a Democratic candidate had tried to buy such coverage. But the news media provided it free of charge, fanned by the commentary of lawmakers and intelligence officials such as Brennan and former National Intelligence Director James Clapper, whose public comments contrasted with the secret intelligence. As the "Impeach Trump" machine raged with fuel provided by Democrats and an errant media, a funny thing happened: More than three dozen Republican incumbents in Congress announced they were retiring in 2018, leaving the GOP with a gaping hole in the House that Democrats exploited.
flags: Article is opinion commentary; its characterizations of officials' private statements and of media reports being wrong are the author's claims
Attribution to John Solomon/The Hill inferred from the accompanying tweet and filename; no byline visible in this crop

images.description: Final continuation screenshot of John Solomon's March 25, 2019 opinion column at The Hill, with the opening paragraph highlighted in yellow. The highlighted text claims polls showed about half of American voters believed Trump or his aides had colluded with Russia 'even though they hadn't.' The column concludes that the Russia collusion narrative impacted the 2018 midterm election, followed by an italicized author bio identifying Solomon as an investigative columnist and executive vice president for video at The Hill, a tag list, and share/tweet buttons.
images.text: Polls showed the impact of the Russia coverage on voters. About half of American voters declared they believed Trump or his aides had colluded with Russia, even though they hadn't. It is the most compelling proof in a long time that false information repeated long enough becomes truth for many people. Although we are still coming to grips with the finality of the Mueller report, one thing has become increasingly clear: The Russia collusion narrative — fanned by foreigners, dirty tricksters and a willing media — did, in fact, impact an American election. Not the one in 2016, but the midterm that came two years later. John Solomon is an award-winning investigative journalist whose work over the years has exposed U.S. and FBI intelligence failures before the Sept. 11 attacks, federal scientists' misuse of foster children and veterans in drug experiments, and numerous cases of political corruption. He serves as an investigative columnist and executive vice president for video at The Hill. images.description: Screenshot of an opinion article by J.R. Dunn defending Attorney General Jeff Sessions, with red underlines and a red box added to highlight the claim that Peter Schweizer's 2011 book 'Throw Them All Out' found Sessions the only member of Congress free of corruption allegations. The article argues this is why Trump chose Sessions for the Department of Justice, praises his by-the-book handling of Andrew McCabe's firing, and rebuts conservatives who dismiss Sessions as 'part of the swamp'. An inset photo shows Sessions gesturing while testifying, captioned 'A.G. Sessions'. Filename: 'Trust Sessions.png'.
images.text: By J.R. Dunn. Back in 2011, the indomitable Peter Schweizer published Throw Them All Out, a detailed examination of political corruption as it is actually practiced in the halls of Congress. In his investigation, Schweizer found one single member of Congress against whom no allegations could be held - who had never taken a dime that was not his, had never cut any backroom deals, had never, simply put, played the game. That individual was Jeff Sessions. That fact is all you need to know to understand why Donald Trump selected Sessions for the Department of Justice, and why Sessions has followed the course he has in taking on the "Russia collusion" coup effort. Sessions is the quintessential Eagle Scout. He will follow the rules down to the last subclause and will not make his move until every "t" has been crossed and every "i" dotted. We saw the first results of this approach last Friday - in dealing with Andrew McCabe, this century's prime example of a "cookie full of arsenic." A.G. Sessions. Sessions waited until the FBI's Office of Professional Responsibility (which is run by Assistant Director Candice Will, who was appointed by Robert Mueller, of all people) recommended that McCabe be fired. He then had McCabe officially informed beforehand, following established procedure to the letter. This comes under the rubric of "strategy," a concept unfortunately foreign to too many active conservatives. A large number of cons recognize only one course of action: a headlong charge against the closest target while howling at the top of their lungs. Not only do they dismiss any more subtle form of action, but they often attack those engaging in it of cowardice or corruption, or of being an "Alinskyite-Obamaist commie stooge" - despite the fact that their kamikaze runs usually end up heading over the nearest cliff. So it was with Sessions, who has been routinely dismissed as "paid off," being "asleep under his desk," or as "part of the swamp."
flags: Article's claims (Schweizer's finding, 'coup effort' framing) are the author's assertions, not verified facts
Red underlines and box are annotations added by whoever shared the screenshot

images.description: Dark-theme screenshot of Q drop 3429 (tripcode !!mG7VJxZNCI, 15 Jul 2019), as rendered by a Q-drop aggregator app, titled with the question of whether the Manhattan power outage was an attempt to 'takeout' Jeffrey Epstein. The drop poses rhetorical questions about eliminating a liability, where Epstein is held, coincidences, and 'POWERful people connected', ending with 'PANIC.' It links the July 13 2019 Manhattan blackout to Epstein's detention without evidence.
images.text: 3429. Was the Manhattan Power Outage an Attempt to Takeout Epstein?. Q !!mG7VJxZNCI 15 Jul 2019 - 5:47:53 AM. How do you eliminate a LIABILITY?. Where is EPSTEIN being held?. Reconcile. Do you believe in coincidences?. POWERful people connected?. PANIC. Q
flags: The drop's implied link between the Manhattan blackout and Epstein is an unverified claim; officials attributed the July 13 2019 outage to equipment failure

images.description: Photograph, apparently a still shot taken through a window or from drone footage, of a room interior with a bare, stained mattress set on a dark platform beneath a large sliding glass window that looks directly out over open water. Metal scaffolding poles stand in the right foreground, and crumpled white sheeting or plastic lies at the head of the mattress, giving the room an under-renovation or abandoned look. In the context of Q drop 3493 (July 2019) this image circulated as showing the interior of a building on Jeffrey Epstein's Little St. James Island, imagery widely attributed to drone footage of the island; the location is not identifiable from the image itself.
flags: Location claim (interior on Epstein's island) comes from the drop's context and circulation, not from anything visible in the image — unverified

The video title identifies the location as Little St. James Island, U.S. Virgin Islands (Jeffrey Epstein's island), filmed by drone in July 2019; the structure's flat green top appears painted or tarped. Playback bar shows 2:14 of 4:51.
images.text: 2:14 / 4:51. cleaned by Adbloc. dophile Island, Little St. James USVI Drone July 2019 4 (1/2)

images.description: Aerial/drone still of a teal-green painted recessed doorway with louvered double doors, sunk below grade into a dry scrub-covered hillside and reached by a dirt path; low green retaining walls flank the sunken entry. The frame matches widely circulated July 2019 drone footage of Little St. James Island, U.S. Virgin Islands (Jeffrey Epstein's island), where the structure was presented online as a possible bunker or tunnel entrance. images.description: Screenshot of a Windows application titled 'Pepe Island Test' — a retro pixel-art point-and-click adventure game in the style of classic LucasArts titles. A Pepe the Frog character in a red shirt stands on a grassy island path near a small hole and a wooden signpost reading 'TENNIS', with hills, palm trees, a road and the sea behind. A verb menu bar (WALK, LOOK, INTERACT, TALK, INVENTORY) runs across the top, and the location name 'Rabbit Hole' is displayed at upper right.
images.text: Pepe Island Test. WALK. LOOK. INTERACT. TALK. INVENTORY. Rabbit Hole. TENNIS.

images.description: Screenshot of Q post #3325 (tripcode Q !!mG7VJxZNCI, ID 78db02, No.6316088, dated Apr 25 2019 20:20:28 EST). The post asks why a President of the United States — referring to Barack Obama by the nickname 'HUSSEIN' — would be assigned 'RENEGADE' as his Secret Service codename, then quotes a dictionary definition of 'renegade' as a person who deserts and betrays an organization, country, or set of principles. 'Renegade' was in fact Obama's Secret Service codename; the post's insinuation of betrayal is the drop's claim.
images.text: Q !!mG7VJxZNCI ID: 78db02 No.6316088. 3325. Apr 25 2019 20:20:28 (EST). Why would a President of the United States [HUSSEIN] assign 'RENEGADE' as his USSS codename? Define 'Renegade'. noun. 1. a person who deserts and betrays an organization, country, or set of principles. synonyms: traitor, defector, deserter, turncoat, betrayer; adjective: renegade. 1. having treacherously changed allegiance. Q
flags: The post's implication that the codename signifies betrayal is the drop's claim; Secret Service codenames are chosen for practical use, not as character judgments

images.description: Dark-themed screenshot of Q post #1429 (tripcode Q !CbboFOtcZs, 20 May 2018) as displayed in a Q aggregator app, headed with the aggregator-supplied title 'Loretta Fuddy Plane Crash Death & Obama Birth Certificate Cover-up'. The drop states 'The Truth has been in front of you the entire time' and links to a Donald Trump tweet. The title connects Loretta Fuddy, the Hawaii health director who verified Barack Obama's birth certificate and died in a 2013 plane crash, to a claimed cover-up; that connection is the aggregator/drop's claim.
images.text: 1429. Loretta Fuddy Plane Crash Death & Obama Birth Certificate Cover-up. Q !CbboFOtcZs 20 May 2018 - 3:06:04 PM. The Truth has been in front of you the entire time. https://twitter.com/realDonaldTrump/status/411247268763676673. Q
flags: The 'cover-up' framing and the linkage of Fuddy's death to Obama's birth certificate are unverified claims made by the drop title; Fuddy's 2013 death was ruled a cardiac arrhythmia after a crash. The headline title is added by the aggregator app, not part of the original drop
